Umbrasas / LRT Lithuania has resumed negotiations with the Taiwanese Representative Office on an economic cooperation action plan following a change in government, the Foreign Ministry said. The talks were temporarily suspended in June as the new Social Democrat-led government restructured the cabinet. The ministry said strengthening economic cooperation with Taiwan remains a long-term foreign policy priority and that Lithuania aims to sign an economic cooperation action plan once negotiations are completed. According to the ministry, the plan is focused on building sustainable economic ties and supporting the development of Lithuaniaâs high-tech sectors. It declined to disclose specific details while consultations are ongoing. The ministry said Lithuaniaâs position on Taiwan remains unchanged and that it seeks to deepen practical cooperation in areas of mutual benefit, including trade, business, education, science, culture and people-to-people exchanges. Officials had previously hoped to finalise the action plan by the end of May and sign it in June before the negotiations were paused. Lithuania and Taiwan have sought to deepen economic ties since the Taiwanese Representative Office opened in Vilnius in 2021. At the time, Lithuanian officials expressed hopes that the move would lead to stronger investment and commercial cooperation. More recently, however, some Lithuanian officials have voiced frustration over what they say has been a slower-than-expected pace of Taiwanese investment. The opening of the representative office triggered a sharp deterioration in relations between Lithuania and China. Beijing viewed the decision to allow the office to use the name âTaiwaneseâ rather than the more common âTaipeiâ as support for Taiwanâs efforts to assert greater international standing. In most countries, similar offices operate under the name âTaipeiâ. LRT English Newsletter Every Friday morning. Thanks for subscribing! Beállítom Egy év alatt hatalmas növekedést ért el Világi Oszkár magán biztonsági cége, az Inrimas Kft. A személy- és objektumvédelmi szolgáltatásokat nyújtó vállalkozás árbevétele tavaly meghaladta a hárommilliárd forintot, ami több mint hússzoros növekedést jelent az előző évhez képest. A cég állami megbízásokból is gazdagodott, Szijjártó Péter idejében a Külgazdasági és Külügyminisztérium több olyan megállapodást is kötött az Inrimas Kft.-vel, amelyek ma is érvényben vannak – írta a 24.hu . A 2023-ban alapított cég volt kommandósokat, egykori katonákat és exlégiósokat alkalmaz, és a 24.hu információja szerint saját technikával és fegyverekkel részt vettek a befuccsolt csádi misszió előkészítésében is. Nem sokkal az alapítás után Világi Oszkár, a Mol-csoport vezérigazgató-helyettese, a szlovákiai Slovnaft korábbi vezére lett a cég tulajdonosa. Világi a Győri ETO és a dunaszerdahelyi DAC futballcsapatok tulajdonosa is egyben, legutóbb pedig azzal került be a hírekbe, hogy Orbán Viktor volt miniszterelnök társaságában bukkant fel egy szerbiai fesztiválon . Az Inrimas és a külügyminisztérium kapcsolatáról Suha György külpolitikai szakértő, volt miniszteri biztos írt korábban a Facebook-oldalán . A korrupciós bűncselekményekkel vádolt Suha beszámolt arról, hogy a cég 2023 óta biztonsági szolgáltatást nyújt a magyar külügynek, embereik több afrikai és ázsiai magyar nagykövetségen látnak el biztosítási feladatokat. Az Orbán Anita vezette Külügyminisztérium megerősítette, hogy valóban van több, máig érvényben lévő megállapodásuk Világi cégével. A 24.hu cikke szerint a minisztérium későbbre ígért részletes választ a szerződések tartalmáról és pénzügyi feltételeiről. A cég ügyvezető igazgatója, Kerékgyártó József – aki korábban a MÁV Start Zrt. vezérigazgatója volt – azt közölte, hogy „a megbízóival fennálló szerződések titoktartásra vonatkozó szabályai” miatt nem adhatnak ki információt az általuk nyújtott szolgáltatásokról. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c3r0.text: Image source, Imago via Alamy Image caption, The arson attack has long been seen as one of the worst attacks targeting Germany's post-war Jewish community By Paul Kirby Europe digital editor Published 5 hours ago German investigators believe they have now identified an arsonist who set fire to a Jewish community centre in Munich in 1970, killing seven people. For decades the man's identity remained a mystery. But Munich prosecutors now believe he was a 25-year-old lone neo-Nazi with known antisemitic opinions. The seven killed were all Holocaust survivors aged 59 to 71. Another 15 people were injured. The prosecutors' revelations come too late to secure justice for the victims. The suspect, identified by Der Spiegel magazine as Bernd V, died in 2020. At about 20:40 on 13 February 1970, prosecutors say the killer poured petrol into the wooden stairwell at a retirement home housed inside the Jewish community building on Reichenbachstrasse, and then set it alight. The fire spread quickly to the top floor of the building. While many managed to escape to the roof or were rescued by firefighters, four of the victims died in the stairwell and another died after jumping from a window. Prosecutors now believe they have "compelling grounds pointing to the (deceased) suspect being the perpetrator", based on "credible information" from a woman, who came forward last year after the death of a close relative who had known the man well. According to prosecutors, the suspected killer was heard to claim within the immediate vicinity of the community building that "the Jews had everything" and he wanted to "set them on fire". Fifteen minutes later, the building was engulfed in flames. Authorities say those remarks have been corroborated by other members of the witness's family. They say other witnesses described the man as having a "Hitler-fixation" - and how he had listened to records of speeches by the Nazi dictator in his youth. One head teacher told them the suspect had apparently used a Hitler-youth dagger, given to him by his father, during a confrontation. He was later given a juvenile conviction for blowing up two phone kiosks. Spiegel reports that the female witness's relative had once been a member of a gang of burglars and that on the night of the arson attack on the retirement home they had taken part in a failed raid on a jewellery store in nearby GÃ¤rtnerplatz. The relative said the botched burglary had infuriated Bernd V and stirred him into an antisemitic rage. The investigation into the arson attack was closed in 2017 because of a lack of conclusive evidence, before being re-opened last year. Prosecutors say the presumption of innocence still applies, even after a suspect's death, and they have also said there is no reliable evidence to suggest anyone else was involved in the attack. Fifty-six years later, German authorities are now confident they have cracked a notorious antisemitic crime. However, the case will quite likely be seen as a historic failure by police. Bernd V's name had been brought to the attention of investigators in the early 1970s, according to Spiegel by a man who shared a prison cell with him. But they had insufficient evidence and dropped the case against him some time afterwards. https://business-review.eu/tech/cognizan.text: Cognizant builds the future through the “Cognizant Future Talent in Tech Romania” initiative Cognizant Romania, one of the largest technology centers in Eastern Europe of the American Cognizant group (NASDAQ: CTSH), with more than 2,500 employees in Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca, Iași, Timișoara and Baia Mare, launches Cognizant Future Talent in Tech Romania, an initiative through which the company supports education as a foundation for the future of young people in Romania. The program brings together three projects with different impact and needs, run by Asociația pentru Valori în Educație (“AVE”), Asociația Creștină Something New and Asociația Casa Bună, with a direct impact on more than 860 beneficiaries and an indirect impact on more than 4,000 people across the country, as well as on the communities around them. The initiative starts from the belief that in a world shaped by AI and rapid change, young people need relevant education, access to resources, and adults ready to guide them. From potential to real opportunities: education as the infrastructure of the future Read more about LIH Group returns to positive gross profit after the first half of 2026 and focuses its strategic growth around insurance read more Romania is living a real paradox. It is recognized worldwide for the quality of its IT talent, being considered a true „Silicon Valley” of Eastern Europe, yet at the same time there are significant digital skills gaps within the general population. Just over half of young Romanians aged 16 to 24 (53.3%) have at least basic digital skills, according to 2025 Eurostat data, compared to the European Union average of 74.6%, with Romania ranking second-to-last in the EU on this indicator. Between these two realities lies a space where education can change the trajectory of people’s lives. A space where Cognizant Romania chooses to step in, through three projects that do not treat education as a one-off intervention, but as a long-term investment in people, communities, and Romania’s capacity to remain relevant in an increasingly digital economy. „When we support education, we are not only investing in a possible future for the tech industry, but in the possibility for young people to have real options, in a Romania where technology is changing the way we learn. For us, Cognizant Future Talent in Tech Romania is about responsibility, trust, and about how our team, used to building solutions for the future, can contribute to the communities it is part of. We start from the fact that our country already has a good reputation in the industry and has talent in the technology field, and we consciously choose to also develop the generation that will carry it forward, in the new era of technology shaped by AI. Cognizant has the global mission of building the future of technology from the position of an AI Builder, and chooses to support continuous education precisely because we understand that it represents the foundation young people need to build their own path, in line with today’s increasingly dynamic realities”, said Mihai Constandiș, Country Manager & Head of Romania Studios. Cognizant Future Talent in Tech Romania is a long-term initiative. For 2026, the investment amounts to more than 500,000 USD, support provided both through the state’s fiscal sponsorship mechanism, which allows the redirection of 20% of corporate income tax to NGOs, and through the direct contribution of Cognizant specialists to the development of the Polaris application within the AVE project. The three projects cover complementary stages: Educational recovery, trust and inclusion through the NGO Casa Buna The project run by Casa Buna addresses one of the most urgent educational needs: closing learning gaps before they become permanent barriers. Through 13 remedial education camps held during the 2026 and 2027 school holidays, 100 children aged 5 to 14 from vulnerable communities in Ferentari, Jilava and Arges County will benefit from intensive literacy and math sessions with psycho-emotional support and healthy life routines. At the same time, the program trains a team of at least 20 students and volunteers in remedial education, who can continue to support the children after the camps end. Modern education where infrastructure is lacking, through the NGO Something New Through EDUBus, a mobile lab equipped with laptops, robotics kits and virtual reality sets, the project brings modern education to seven villages in Cluj and Salaj counties. The program combines STEM sessions, critical thinking workshops, educational camps and digital parenting sessions, for a community of 500 children, 150 mothers and 36 teachers who would otherwise not have had access to these resources. Polaris – technology for the leadership of the school of the future, through the NGO Asociatia pentru Valori in Educatie Asociația pentru Valori în Educatie (AVE) is relaunching the School Management and Leadership Academy (ALMS), the leadership accelerator dedicated to school principals, which combines experiential learning, approaches from the startup world, and mentoring from corporate and entrepreneurial professionals to help them increase their impact in schools. Polaris is the digital platform that extends the ALMS experience, supporting a continuous, personalized and measurable leadership development journey. Integrated into the principal’s learning path, Polaris uses artificial intelligence to support reflection and guidance, helping principals see their progress more clearly and suggesting relevant directions for development. The platform is developed with the financial support of Cognizant and the direct contribution of a team of Cognizant Romania engineers and professionals, based on principles of explainable and responsible AI. https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2026/.text: As a chick, he fell out of the nest. Local residents and staff at the Masurian Landscape Park rescued him. Later he was released back into the wild. Since then, thanks to a GPS transmitter, thousands of people have been following his journey. On 16 August he set off on his next tour.That morning (18.08) the GPS transmitter once again reported Krutek's position. The stork was already about 70 kilometres east of Lviv, in the Zolochiv area of Ukraine.Family first, then AfricaThis year's season was something special for Krutek. The well-known stork became a father for the first time. Five chicks hatched in his nest. Sadly, one did not survive. Under the watchful eyes of their parents, four young birds grew up and in July began their first attempts at flying.The youngsters fledged and the nest became cramped. Apparently the parents decided it was time for more space.Krutek and his partner therefore started on a new nest, a few dozen metres away from the old one.Nevertheless, Krutek did not neglect his family duties. He continued to look after the youngsters and bring them food. During this time the young storks practised flying with great enthusiasm.Now heading southOn 16 August Krutek set off on his next journey. Ornithologists do not yet know whether this time he will follow exactly the same route as on his previous migrations. That is precisely what makes his GPS track so fascinating at the moment.The transmitter shows where the bird stops to rest, how fast he covers each leg of the journey and whether he uses his tried-and-tested stopover sites again. In recent years his route has taken him past the Bosphorus, among other places, and he has spent the winter in Egypt. All told, around 5,000 kilometres lie ahead of Krutek.In spring he makes headlinesKrutek has already completed a long journey this year. In February he returned from Africa to Poland, but the homecoming did not go smoothly. Passing pedestrians found the exhausted bird on a road near Jedwabno and came to his aid. Rangers then took him into their care and brought him to the stork protection centre in Krutyń. He covered the final stretch back to his traditional nest... by car.Later he made a full recovery, resumed looking after the nest and embarked on his most prolific breeding season so far.A stork with his own fan baseIt is hardly surprising that Krutek is now regarded as an avian star. His arrival in Poland is one of the first harbingers of spring.These days you could say that Krutek has something many travellers would envy him for – an audience of his own that checks every year to see where in the world he is.This time the answer is: on the move.Experts are wishing him tailwinds, good thermals and a safe journey. And we can only assume that the stork knows exactly what he is doing; after all, he has more travel experience than many a holidaymaker behind the wheel.Have a good trip, Krutek. See you in Masuria in the spring.
